messages:
maria: heads up — noticed a cluster of short gaps in SSE streams around 11:12 UTC for a handful of tenants. gaps look like: client reconnect -> no resume events for ~20-40s -> resume with repeated tokens. dashboard: https://console/redwood/streams?panel=gap-rate :warning:
josh: can you paste a log example and the tenant id?
maria: tenant=acct-42, route=eu-west-1/shard-7. log excerpt:
```
2026-03-20T11:12:03Z INFO stream: keepalive missed route=eu-west-1/shard-7 session_id=sh_abc last_event_id=evt_987
2026-03-20T11:12:25Z WARN stream: gap_detected route=eu-west-1/shard-7 gap_ms=22000
2026-03-20T11:12:40Z INFO stream: client_reconnect session_id=sh_abc resume_token=tok_foo result=resume_success
```
kevin: that gap window matches our route-aging TTL (30s) + proxy reattachment window. My hypothesis: proxy evicts sticky route entry after idle, new attach creates a fresh route until resume path reconciles, which generates duplicate accounting spikes. :thinking_face:
anne: agree. two pieces: (1) telemetry is too coarse to tell if resume was routed to same shard instance, (2) console lacks route-age visibility for the session. We should add metric labels: `route_age_seconds` and `route_instance` to streaming_gap_count and resume_success histograms.
sre-bot: [ALERT] streaming-gap-rate high for acct-42 (5m avg > 3/min). Incident ticket #INC-2026-113 created.
maria: UX ask — can we surface route age and last_route_instance in the Streams page for an individual session? Right now operators can't tell if a resume hit a different backend. :eyes:
josh: short-term mitigation: increase sticky route TTL from 30s -> 60s with jitter and add a fallback that treats resume within 90s + same last_event_id as same session for billing attribution. Need perf/telemetry to confirm no increased hot-shard pressure.
kevin: adding TTL is reasonable but we must capture `route_claim_count` and `route_reassign_count` to watch for hot-shard thrash. Also capture `resume_latency_ms{same_instance=true|false}` so we can validate user impact.
anne: client library patch suggestion — accept a `prefer_resume_same_route` flag that prefers TCP routing header if client knows last_route_instance (we can return that in resume_success). snippet to add to client: ```js
const headers = { 'x-last-route': lastRoute || '' }
fetch(streamUrl, { headers })
```
maria: cool. I'll write the console change to show last_route in session trace + a small note in rollout doc. Can we canary the TTL bump 5% traffic for 8h? :shipit:
josh: yes — 5% for 8h then check metrics: streaming-gap-rate, route_reassign_count, resume_latency_ms. I'll open a rollout PR and link tests.
sre-bot: deploy job started: deploy/streaming-proxy:ttl-bump-2026-03-20 (canary 5%). CI build: https://ci/redwood/2345
kevin: updated dashboard queries — added those labels and a panel for resume_latency by same_instance. Ping me if the histogram splits weirdly.
maria: thanks everyone. will follow up with a short postmortem if gaps persist. :thumbsup:
